implementations.roadmap_assessment: Recent shipped changes already address query-planning and cache issues; no vendor speedup is transferred to our workload. Streaming follow-up is announced without a delivery guarantee; no broader roadmap commitment assumed.

primer.strongest_challenge: An honest bounded stop can still be misread as a comparative win for the existing ordering or completed retrieval evaluation. The clean receipt contains zero timed observations for A/B/C and no paired deltas; first-warm-up failure therefore supports deferring qualification only. It cannot establish a warm latency distribution, relative ordering quality, or that pre-rerank expansion fails. The mandatory comparison task remains [ ] while AC-4 is [~], so final task reconciliation must preserve the same explicit noncompletion.
primer.best_alternative: Accept a bounded, explicitly unqualified AC-4 deferral; retain current ordering as the operational default and preserve the frozen protocol, hashes, empty comparison summaries and excluded historical attempts. Reconcile the matching comparison task to [~] with the same rationale when finalizing scope. In the ADR state that no variant was evaluated and no speed/quality preference was measured. Any later attempt must be a separately authorized evaluation with declared prerequisites, independent full relevance/actual-edge judgments, frozen providers and a fresh paired run; do not relax this run retroactively. This yields an auditable decision at negligible additional compute cost, at the tradeoff of leaving the potential retrieval improvement unknown.

thinking_stances_applied.analogical: Treat this like an interrupted preregistered trial: preserve original stopping rules and censored outcome, distinguish run disposition from intervention efficacy, and start a new protocol for future changed conditions.

findings.area: SqlGraph public methods and shared publication
findings.finding: Lazy graph methods perform multiple independent autocommit SELECTs; they do not acquire one read snapshot across traversal. A concurrent commit can mix topology/metadata generations even though shared_probes demonstrates explicit r BEGIN correctness.
findings.fix: Either use a whole-query read transaction with concurrency probes or explicitly leave lazy-API concurrent snapshot parity unqualified. Do not infer from database transaction demonstration that prototype serving preserves current immutable GraphQueryIndex snapshot.

findings.finding: Resource guard reads RUSAGE_SELF and omits active child RSS. startup_samples and shared_probes spawn children, and os._exit only terminates parent. snapshot creates/copies before any resource guard. MEM_CAP/host_memory are hardcoded host provenance.
findings.fix: Use aggregate owned-process RSS and stop owned descendants; establish budget before snapshot writes or disclose capture outside resource qualification. Detect/verify physical RAM or explicitly scope harness to qualified 32GiB host. Coordinator serializes configurations; ensure all harnesses honor same lock.

findings.finding: External-bridge oracle is asserted only for A, not B. Confidence fixture uses only high-confidence call alternatives, so 1-vs-2 call cost and confidence filtering not independently exercised. Safety mutant test merely asserts bypass returns REPO, then labels mutant detected without running a validator against it.
findings.fix: Run external bridge fixture through both backends; add tiny hand-derived competing extracted/resolved routes and confidence cutoff. Replace mutant claim with actual assertion that rejects injected bypass, or remove mutation-validation claim.

findings.finding: Default seeds are outgoing-call symbols, reused for imports and inheritance; these may return zero hits. Weighted paths pair unrelated seed names and may all be not-found. Raw receipts retain latency but not result sizes/found counts. No graph_impact/risk/report, doc-link or path-prefix workload is executed, although source-level algorithm reuse does not guarantee adapter parity.
findings.fix: Use relation-specific nonempty seeds and known reachable weighted pairs; record result size/found/truncated. Inventory and explicitly mark missing families unqualified or add bounded probes before claiming native full parity. Root's separate queries manifest may repair timing seed selection; evidence must retain and hash it.

findings.finding: Cache invalidation wraps traverse/one_hop/shortest_path only; graph_impact/risk/report can use stale cached adjacency after a commit. External-supertype index is never refreshed. 8MiB cache estimate counts serialized JSON length, not Python resident object allocation.
findings.fix: Keep H experimental/unqualified outside these methods; distinguish serialized-payload budget from actual measured RSS. Invalidate at every public query boundary and rebuild derived indexes for production.

findings.finding: Mapping uses one source location and LIMIT20, records only count, and makes no nonzero assertion. A zero-row join would not fail shared_probes. This cannot establish symbol/chunk multiplicity, coverage or ownership correctness.
findings.fix: Require nonempty known mapping fixtures plus hand-derived zero/one/many chunk mappings; report count-only query as illustrative join, not mapping qualification.

findings.finding: Startup excludes interpreter imports; publication changes one prepared node and excludes extraction/re-resolution; A update includes reconstructing full graph while SQL does one node lookup; full prepared persistence omits C; scale is one A-then-B process with shared RSS. These are valid prototype measurements only.
findings.fix: Keep explicit labels and exclude these from real whole-tool, full rebuild, total deployment footprint or C adoption gates. Missing public integration and global algorithm measurements remain unqualified.
